findings.title: IPC deadlock: ping_srv -> pong_srv -> ping_srv (2 threads in a wait-for cycle, 2 more blocked behind it)
findings.root_cause: Threads ping_srv (waiting to send, priority 20); pong_srv (waiting to send, priority 20) are blocked on each other in a cycle: each is inside a message handler and made a blocking MsgSend() to a channel whose only server thread is itself blocked, so none of them can reach MsgReceive() again. Clients blocked behind the cycle: client1, client2. They stayed blocked for 1206 ms in this trace. Evidence: events #7396, #7397, #7398, #7399.
findings.fix: Never make a blocking MsgSend() to another server from inside a handler while the original client is still waiting for a reply. Either (1) reply to the client first and then notify the peer with a pulse (MsgSendPulse, never blocks), (2) hand the nested call to a worker thread, (3) impose a global call order between servers so cycles cannot form, or (4) at minimum arm TimerTimeout() on the nested call and handle ETIMEDOUT.
